name: Chloe Whitfield
presenting_complaint: Deliberate paracetamol overdose, uncertain amount and timing

medical_history.social: University student, lives in share-house. Recent relationship breakdown. Drinks alcohol occasionally; no regular alcohol excess. Non-smoker.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 22-year-old woman is brought to ED by a friend after taking 'a lot of Panadol' following a relationship breakdown. She thinks she took tablets across the afternoon and evening, possibly the first dose around 6-8 hours ago and more since, so the ingestion is staggered and the exact timing is unclear. She is alert (GCS 15) and haemodynamically stable with normal observations, but tearful and expressing ongoing suicidal thoughts. Obs: BP 112/70, HR 92, RR 16, SpO2 99% RA, afebrile.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: Full overdose risk assessment: exact agent(s), total dose ingested (mg and mg/kg), time of first and last dose, single versus STAGGERED ingestion, and time over which taken
Co-ingestants (especially other paracetamol-containing/combination products, alcohol, sertraline) and any modified-release paracetamol taken
Intent and ongoing suicidality: current suicidal ideation, plan, note prior self-harm and precipitant (relationship breakdown)
Risk factors for hepatotoxicity: chronic alcohol excess, malnutrition/eating disorder, enzyme-inducing drugs, fasting state
Symptom screen: nausea, vomiting, right upper quadrant pain (often asymptomatic early); pregnancy possibility
Document medications, allergies and collateral history from the friend
objective: Timed serum paracetamol level: at 4 hours post-ingestion if a single known time, or IMMEDIATELY on arrival because the ingestion is staggered/uncertain-time (do not wait to reach an arbitrary 4-hour mark)
Baseline bloods: LFTs (ALT/AST), INR/coags, UEC/creatinine, venous blood gas (pH, bicarbonate, lactate), BGL, salicylate level and serum beta-hCG
Repeat/serial paracetamol level and ALT/INR to track (e.g. at 8-hourly intervals during NAC per protocol)
Examination: hydration, GCS/conscious level, RUQ tenderness, signs of hepatic dysfunction; continuous monitoring
Weigh the patient (or estimate weight) for weight-based NAC dosing
assessment: Deliberate paracetamol overdose with STAGGERED / uncertain-time ingestion — treat as high-risk for hepatotoxicity regardless of a single reassuring pre-4-hour level

Risk of hepatotoxicity/acute liver failure if N-acetylcysteine delayed; interpret single-timepoint level on the paracetamol treatment nomogram ONLY when time is known and ingestion is a single acute overdose
High acute mental-health risk: active suicidal ideation requiring psychiatric assessment before disposition
Consider co-ingestant toxicity (salicylate, serotonergic effects) as differentials
plan: Phone the Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26 and follow the current Australian paracetamol poisoning guideline (FIRST action)

Start N-acetylcysteine EMPIRICALLY now because ingestion is staggered/uncertain-time — do NOT wait for the level. AMH 3-bag IV regimen: 150 mg/kg in 200 mL 5% glucose over 15-60 min, then 50 mg/kg over 4 h, then 100 mg/kg over 16 h (many centres use the 2-bag regimen 200 mg/kg over 4 h then 100 mg/kg over 16 h)
Activated charcoal 50 g PO only if presentation is very early (within ~1-2 h of a significant ingestion), airway protected, and on senior/PIC advice
IV access, fluids to maintain hydration, antiemetic (e.g. ondansetron 4 mg IV) as needed
Continue NAC until criteria met: paracetamol level below the treatment line AND ALT normal/not rising AND INR normal — do not stop on a single level alone
Escalate to toxicology/ICU and discuss with a liver unit if rising INR, encephalopathy, acidosis (pH <7.3) or creatinine rise (King's College criteria)
Formal mental-health/psychiatric risk assessment and 1:1 nursing/observation before any disposition; ensure safety and remove means
Serial LFTs, INR and paracetamol levels; monitor for NAC anaphylactoid reaction (slow/pause infusion, give antihistamine, then restart)

critical_errors: Waiting for a paracetamol level before starting NAC when the timing is unclear or the ingestion is staggered — NAC must be started empirically
Relying on a single pre-4-hour paracetamol level to withhold treatment (levels before 4 hours post-ingestion cannot exclude toxicity)
Discharging or making a disposition decision without a formal mental-health/suicide risk assessment
must_not_miss: Timely N-acetylcysteine for staggered/uncertain-time ingestion (do not delay)
Staggered ingestion recognised — nomogram not applicable, treat empirically
Active suicidality assessed and patient kept safe before disposition
Escalation criteria for acute liver failure (rising INR, encephalopathy, acidosis) considered
